Large payloads through the broker: 256KB caps everywhere (SQS, EventBridge, OCI Queue); claim-check (payload in object store, pointer in event) is the prescribed pattern; FOQS caps items at 10KB.
Exposing raw queues to external callers: AWS wraps every internal queue behind lightweight authenticated APIs that stamp caller identity before enqueue.
Monitoring queue depth instead of oldest-message age as the backlog signal.

Kafka-as-multi-tenant-SaaS-substrate without isolation primitives: tenancy via 'operational discipline and cluster segmentation' (per-team clusters) is the documented Kafka weakness Pulsar was built to fix; Kafka adding KIP-932 'Queues for Kafka' is a late admission that log-only semantics don't cover the queue shape.
DeadLetterPolicy combined with Pulsar transactions (documented incompatibility — use negative-ack within transactions).

Single product stretched across all three shapes: Azure's published rationale for the 3-way split is precisely that telemetry logs, priceless messages, and discrete events have irreconcilable delivery contracts.
oyatie_prescriptions: Pulsar choice is VALIDATED, keep it as launch-primary: its tenant->namespace->topic hierarchy, namespace rate quotas, bookie-affinity groups, broker isolation policies, and stateless-broker rebalancing are exactly the in-broker multi-tenant isolation Kafka lacks; proven at Yahoo (100B+ msg/day, 1.4M topics, <5ms avg publish) and Tencent Midas billing (tens of billions of financial txns/day, 99.999% availability) — the Midas case is a direct existence proof for Oyatie's events-as-billing architecture on this exact substrate.

Ship the convergent trichotomy as THREE single-concern Rust/axum surface services over ONE Pulsar substrate (per ADR-0132 no-grouping): oya-queue (Shared/Key_Shared subscriptions, visibility-timeout-style lease semantics, retry-letter + DLQ topics, redrive API), oya-stream (partitioned topics, cursor/seek replay, tiered storage), oya-bus (rules/pattern routing + push delivery, EventBridge/Event Grid-shaped, CloudEvents 1.0 envelope). Do not run three broker substrates — Pulsar's subscription model and Google's unified Pub/Sub prove one substrate carries all three contracts.

Tenant-keyed partitioning doctrine: ordering key = tenant_id (or tenant_id:aggregate_id) everywhere; one Pulsar namespace per tenant tier/cell; shuffle-shard tenants across broker+bookie cells so a poisoned tenant blast radius is bounded; enforce produce/consume/manage authorization with Cedar policies evaluated at the axum surface (tenant, namespace, topic, action as Cedar entities) layered over Pulsar's native tenant auth.

Exactly-once doctrine (write it into the API contract SSOT): transport is at-least-once, period. Cross-service correctness = transactional outbox in the bespoke distributed-SQL (same Raft-group commit as the business write) + idempotent consumer with inbox dedup keyed on message ID + publish dedup tokens with SQS-style 5-minute windows. Reserve Pulsar transactions exclusively for consume-transform-produce pipelines that start and end inside Pulsar; never promise end-to-end exactly-once in any public contract.

DLQ/replay as a platform-wide invariant: every subscription gets retry-letter topic -> bounded delivery attempts (default 5, max 20 like OCI) -> dead-letter topic -> redrive API; oya-bus gets EventBridge-style archive+replay with replayed events tagged via envelope metadata; backfill via Pulsar cursor rewind on streams. Wire the bespoke CAS object store (W5) in as the Pulsar tiered-storage offloader — write a Rust offloader; sealed immutable BookKeeper segments are content-addressed by nature, a perfect CAS fit, and this makes archive/replay storage free-riding on W5.

Schema governance: CloudEvents 1.0 envelope mandatory on the bus; payload schemas registered in Pulsar's built-in registry with server-side enforcement ON; compatibility default BACKWARD_TRANSITIVE (Oyatie is replay-heavy, so consumers must read ALL historical versions, not just N-1); consumer-first upgrade ordering enforced; AsyncAPI documents checked into the buck2 monorepo as the contract artifact with compatibility checks as cloud-ci admission gates (extend /specs/api-contract-ssot-canonical.json to reference AsyncAPI per topic).

Saga doctrine: orchestration-first for any flow with >=3 compensating steps via a bespoke Rust workflow engine (Step-Functions-class state machine, state persisted in the distributed-SQL substrate — this is a separate research/build item); choreography over oya-bus only for simple notify/fan-out; ban cross-service 2PC in the operating contract.

Backlog operations doctrine (encode as OpenSLO per ADR-0130): primary SLO = oldest-unacked-message age per subscription, NOT backlog depth; consumers must heartbeat/extend ack deadlines on long work (prevent SQS-style fork-bomb redelivery); per-tenant fairness throttling at the oya-queue surface; quarantine/sideline namespaces for poison traffic; tag every async workload with a Meta-style delay-tolerance class (realtime-ms / minutes / hours / days) and schedule dispatch accordingly.

Two explicit loss classes, per Meta's honesty: a never-lose class (billing, audit, outbox-relayed domain events — full BookKeeper fsync, write-quorum 3/ack 2, no retention expiry before warehouse offload confirmation) and a best-effort class (telemetry, logs — relaxed durability, aggressive retention). Billing/metering = events on the never-lose class: every service emits CloudEvents metering records keyed by tenant; aggregation service rolls up hourly per dimension per tenant (AWS MeterUsage shape); audit pipeline is a separate ordered per-tenant stream consumed into the distributed-SQL ledger. Accuracy as design condition: the metering namespace gets the strictest SLO in the platform.

Bespoke-Rust W5 destination (adopt the proven shape, reimplement Rust-native): stateless broker tier + segment-replicated storage tier with journal/entry-log disk separation (BookKeeper-class, client-side replication, immutable sealed segments) + Raft-based embedded metadata (NO external coordinator — learn from KRaft and Oxia; reuse the multi-Raft machinery from the distributed-SQL W5 effort) + subscription-type dispatch (Exclusive/Failover/Shared/Key_Shared) + tiered offload to the bespoke CAS store. Keep Oyatie services on a thin owned client crate abstracting the Pulsar protocol from day one so the W5 swap is a substrate replacement, not an application migration.

Do NOT build: a provisioned-partition 'lite' tier (Pub/Sub Lite died), per-priority features inside one queue (use separate queues/delay-tolerance classes per AWS/Meta practice), global ordering, raw broker endpoints exposed to tenants (always front with the authenticated axum surfaces), or a fourth/fifth broker product.

Engineering budgets from published numbers: per-partition unit economics converge at ~1MB/s write / 2MB/s read (Kinesis shard = OCI partition = Event Hubs TU) — adopt as initial per-partition capacity budget; 99.95% monthly uptime (Pub/Sub SLA) is table-stakes for the messaging surface, 99.999% (Midas) for the billing class; design the queue surface API for horizontal scale-out with no per-queue ceiling (SQS demonstrated 1.66e8 msg/s aggregate; OCI's 10MB/s per-queue cap is the anti-example of a ceiling you don't want).

research.domain: API Gateway + Edge Services + Marketplace + Developer Platform Surface (hyperscaler patterns for Oyatie's owned cloud substrate)

per_company.approach: API Gateway (REST/HTTP/WebSocket): edge-optimized endpoints front with CloudFront; private integrations/VPC links ride Hyperplane — distributed NFV packet-state fabric in production since 2015 (publicly described re:Invent 2017), also powering NLB/PrivateLink/NAT-GW/EFS/Transit Gateway; explicitly multi-tenant with SHUFFLE-SHARDING of nodes to contain noisy neighbors (Builders Library 'Workload isolation using shuffle-sharding'). Throttling is a documented 4-layer token-bucket hierarchy applied in order: per-client/per-method usage-plan limit → per-method stage limit → account-level (default ~10k RPS/region) → AWS regional limit; usage-plan quotas are EXPLICITLY best-effort — docs warn never to rely on them for cost control. Usage plans + API keys are the packaging/monetization unit. AppSync = managed GraphQL with direct/JS resolvers; Merged APIs federate up to 10 source APIs with canonical-type conflict directives and auto-merge. Smithy: protocol-agnostic typed IDL with traits, used internally since 2018 to generate ALL AWS SDKs/CLI on daily release cadence; open-sourced, plus api-models-aws repo publishing every public service model in JSON AST with daily updates. Gateway-as-PEP precedent: Amazon Verified Permissions generates a Cedar-evaluating Lambda authorizer attached to API Gateway (JWT → principal, path+method → action, Cedar policy store decides). Marketplace: listing pipeline 4–8 weeks (FTR 2–4w, listing review 3–7 business days); SaaS integration contract = ResolveCustomer (purchase token → CustomerIdentifier) + GetEntitlements (Entitlement Service) + MeterUsage/BatchMeterUsage (hourly per dimension per customer, 6-hour late window, idempotent submits with exponential backoff); private offers with negotiated pricing/terms + CPPO channel-partner resale; CrowdStrike/Snowflake/Palo Alto/Splunk each crossed $1B lifetime revenue through AWS Marketplace.

GFE is the universal front door (TLS termination, DDoS absorption, global anycast routing — per infrastructure security design doc); GCLB + Identity-Aware Proxy implements BeyondCorp zero trust: authn + IAM/Access-Context-Manager authz enforced AT THE EDGE before any backend byte (access never determined by network location). ESPv2 = Envoy-based gateway: a Config Manager control plane dynamically programs Envoy filters from the Service Management API; deployed as sidecar or reverse proxy — Google retired nginx-based ESPv1 for Envoy. Apigee adapter for Envoy uses Envoy as data plane with Apigee remote service as PDP. Service Infrastructure (Service Control) is the shared admission/metering substrate for ALL Google APIs: Check (admission, results cached 60s client-side) + AllocateQuota (rate limiting — guidance: batching, caching, predictive allocation, ≤1 call/sec per (service, consumer, metric) tuple) + Report (telemetry/billing) — i.e., local buckets with async global reconciliation by design. Apigee hybrid: management-plane/runtime-plane split; Synchronizer polls management plane and propagates config (fail-static); message processors execute policies; distributed quota counters in Cassandra, Redis for distributed rate limiting. API definition: protobuf-first with ~200 numbered AIPs (AIP-121 resource-oriented design, AIP-127 gRPC↔HTTP transcoding, AIP-185 versioning) + open-sourced api-linter; every Google API is gRPC + transcoded REST from one proto. GCP Marketplace: Partner Procurement API (providers.entitlements.approve, account association, lifecycle events) with usage reporting through the SAME Service Control metering API Google's first-party services use.

No public cloud; the developer platform surface is the Graph API on wholly bespoke C++ infrastructure. Edge: Katran (open-sourced 2018) — XDP/eBPF in-kernel L4 forwarding plane using modified Maglev consistent hashing with unequal backend weights; Proxygen (open-sourced) as the L7 HTTP stack for edge/origin proxies. GraphQL invented at Facebook (2012, open-sourced 2015) and powers hundreds of billions of API calls/day — the only hyperscaler where GraphQL IS the primary surface (Thrift for internal RPC). Rate limiting is budget-scored, not fixed-bucket: Platform Rate Limits per app/user token and Business Use Case Rate Limits per page/system-user token over rolling 1-hour windows; usage transparency pushed to developers via X-App-Usage / X-Business-Use-Case-Usage response headers + App Dashboard (Meta evolved away from rigid per-endpoint limits with 2016 page-level rate-limit redesign). Partner onboarding/gating via App Review and access tiers (development → standard/advanced) — review is the trust ratchet, equivalent to marketplace certification.

API Management is the cleanest three-plane model in the industry: management plane (config API), gateway/data plane (proxy + policy execution + telemetry), developer portal as an explicit third 'user plane' (docs, try-it, onboarding, usage data). Policies are a staged pipeline (inbound/backend/outbound/on-error) attached at global/product/API/operation scope; 'Products' bundle APIs with subscriptions/keys as the packaging unit. Self-hosted gateway: the same gateway containerized and federated to the cloud management plane, designed to FAIL STATIC — survives loss of connectivity, persists a last-known-good config backup on a persistent volume. Azure Front Door: 150+ POPs, BGP anycast + split TCP, primary/fallback edge rings (note: Microsoft is migrating Front Door DNS anycast→unicast through March–April 2026 — operational anycast lesson). TypeSpec: open-source TypeScript-like API definition language with an emitter plugin architecture (OpenAPI, client/server codegen); declared the long-term direction with AutoRest (OpenAPI-first codegen) DEPRECATED effective July 1, 2026; azure-rest-api-specs treats TypeSpec as source and OpenAPI as emitted projection. Commercial marketplace: SaaS Fulfillment APIs v2 — mandatory 24/7 landing page (token resolve → activate), mandatory webhook for async lifecycle events (cancel/plan change), metered-billing API for usage dimensions; certification policies make API integration a listing requirement.

OCI API Gateway: regional gateways living in a VCN subnet (public or private), consolidating backends (LBs, compute, OCI Functions) behind one endpoint; serverless-function backends first-class. Usage plans are the most explicitly modeled monetization resource of the five: a usage plan contains ENTITLEMENTS, each = {rate limit (RPS), quota (per minute→month), target API deployments — spannable across multiple gateways}, bound to subscriber resources holding client tokens. Oracle Cloud Marketplace: requires Oracle Partner Network membership (Level 1+ for transactable listings); paid listings get assigned SKU + meter + unit-of-measure and bill via customer Universal Cloud Credits drawdown (Oracle bills on partner's behalf, 43 countries/local currencies); private offers plus Multi-Party Private Offers (MPPO) for channel/reseller collaboration on a single transaction.

convergent_patterns: Control-plane/data-plane split with push-config + FAIL-STATIC gateway: data plane keeps serving from last-known-good config when the control plane is unreachable (Azure self-hosted gateway persistent-volume config backup; Apigee Synchronizer + message processors; ESPv2 Config Manager → Envoy; Envoy xDS generally). Config flows one way; the hot path never blocks on the control plane.

Envoy as the convergent open proxy substrate at the edge: Google rebuilt ESP on Envoy and ships the Apigee Envoy adapter; Microsoft, Apple, Salesforce, Stripe, eBay, Pinterest, Airbnb, Lyft run it in production; AWS App Mesh used it. The architecture to copy is Envoy's (dynamic xDS config, filter chains, Maglev/ring-hash LB policies) even when the binary is bespoke — Meta and AWS prove the bespoke-binary path.

Two-tier rate limiting everywhere: LOCAL token buckets/counters on each gateway node + ASYNC global aggregation — never a synchronous global counter on the request path. Google Service Control codifies it (60s check cache, batched reports, predictive quota, ≤1 sync/sec per (service,consumer,metric)); Apigee uses distributed counters in Cassandra/Redis; AWS documents usage-plan quotas as best-effort; Meta scores rolling windows. All five accept eventual consistency in exchange for hot-path latency.

Layered throttle hierarchy as explicit policy order: per-client/per-operation (usage plan) → per-operation/stage → per-tenant account → platform/cell limit (AWS documents the exact evaluation order; Azure scopes policies global/product/API/operation; OCI entitlements carry both rate and quota; Apigee separates SpikeArrest (protection) from Quota (monetization)).

API-definition-language-first SDK/server generation, with all three public clouds open-sourcing their IDL: AWS Smithy (all SDKs generated daily since 2018, models published as JSON AST), Google protobuf + AIPs + api-linter (gRPC source, REST transcoded), Microsoft TypeSpec (AutoRest/OpenAPI-first deprecated July 2026). Shared doctrine: the typed IDL is the source; OpenAPI is an EMITTED PROJECTION, never the master; a linter/diff gate enforces design rules and backward compatibility in CI.

The 'API product' as the monetization/packaging unit: a named bundle of operations × {rate, burst, quota period, meters} bound to subscriber keys — AWS usage plans + API keys, Azure APIM products + subscriptions, OCI usage plans + entitlements + subscribers, Apigee API products + developer apps. Four independent reinventions of the same resource model.

Identical marketplace flow at AWS/Azure/GCP/OCI: certified listing pipeline → purchase-token resolve (ResolveCustomer / Azure resolve / GCP account association) → entitlement lifecycle as events/webhooks (GetEntitlements pull + push notifications) → ISV-pushed idempotent metering records (hourly cadence, late-record window, dedupe/retry contract) → cloud-side invoicing and payout. Private offers with negotiated terms + channel/multi-party reseller mechanics (AWS CPPO, Oracle MPPO) exist on all four.

Gateway as policy enforcement point at the edge, backed by an externalized policy engine: Google IAP/BeyondCorp does full user+device authz at the front door; AWS attaches Cedar evaluation (Verified Permissions) to API Gateway via generated authorizer with TTL-cached decisions; Azure validate-jwt + policy pipeline; OCI gateway-level authn/authz. Coarse authn + token validation + policy decision at edge, fine-grained data authz re-checked near the data (BeyondProd defense-in-depth).

Global anycast front door terminating TLS at the POP with split TCP, over a consistent-hashing L4 layer: Google GFE + Maglev, Azure Front Door (150+ POPs, anycast + split TCP, edge rings), AWS CloudFront fronting edge-optimized API Gateway, Meta POPs with Proxygen L7 over Katran XDP/eBPF L4 (modified Maglev).

Developer portal as a first-class plane with self-service keys, generated docs/try-it, and live usage transparency: Azure APIM 'user plane' portal, Apigee developer portals, AWS Marketplace/console + usage plans, Meta App Dashboard plus per-response usage headers (X-App-Usage). Quota state is surfaced TO the developer, not hidden.

Multi-tenant gateway fleets need engineered isolation: AWS shuffle-shards Hyperplane nodes and documents shuffle-sharding as the standard noisy-neighbor defense; cell-based deployment bounds blast radius (Hyperplane per-AZ; Apigee per-runtime-plane; Azure per-instance/region).
divergences: Proxy substrate: Google standardized its gateway data planes on open-source Envoy (ESPv2, Apigee adapter); AWS, Azure, OCI run proprietary gateway fleets (Hyperplane-backed, APIM's own gateway); Meta runs wholly bespoke C++ (Proxygen/Katran). Owning the binary while adopting the architecture is a proven hyperscaler position — validates Oyatie's bespoke-Rust path.

IDL philosophy: Smithy is protocol-agnostic (traits bind protocols later, resource shapes model lifecycles); Google is gRPC/proto-native with REST as transcoding (AIP-127); TypeSpec is OpenAPI-ecosystem-centric with a general emitter framework; Meta splits Thrift (internal RPC) from GraphQL (product surface). No convergence on syntax — only on the source-of-truth + projections + linter doctrine.

GraphQL strategy: Meta made it the primary surface (hundreds of billions of calls/day); AWS productized managed GraphQL with federation (AppSync Merged APIs, canonical-type directives); Google and Azure treat GraphQL as a pass-through/synthetic policy target at the gateway. No public cloud exposes its OWN control plane as GraphQL.

Quota honesty: AWS explicitly documents usage-plan throttles/quotas as best-effort and unsuitable for cost control; OCI markets entitlement quotas as enforceable subscriber controls; Google documents best-effort-with-caching semantics. Same architecture, different contractual framing.

Edge authz depth: Google pushes full identity+device-context authorization to the front door (BeyondCorp/IAP); AWS keeps SigV4/IAM at the platform edge and makes Cedar fine-grained authz an opt-in authorizer hop; Azure delegates depth entirely to policy authors per API.

Marketplace metering substrate: Google reuses the exact Service Control Check/Report/AllocateQuota plane for both first-party APIs and third-party marketplace metering; AWS built dedicated Marketplace Metering + Entitlement services separate from its API platform; Oracle binds marketplace billing to Universal Cloud Credits drawdown. One-substrate (Google) vs dedicated-service (AWS) is a real fork in the road.

Front-door routing: Azure is actively migrating Front Door DNS from anycast to unicast (Mar–Apr 2026) while Google/AWS/Meta remain anycast-committed — anycast at the DNS layer has operational failure modes at least one hyperscaler decided to retire.
anti_patterns: Hand-maintained OpenAPI as the master spec: Microsoft deprecated AutoRest/OpenAPI-first outright (EOL July 1, 2026) in favor of TypeSpec-as-source; AWS never let OpenAPI be the source (Smithy since 2018); Google generates REST from proto. OpenAPI is an output artifact only.

Synchronous global quota/entitlement checks on the request hot path — every published architecture replaces them with local caching + batching + async reconciliation (Service Control's explicit ≤1 RPC/sec guidance; Apigee distributed counters; AWS best-effort buckets).

Relying on gateway quotas as billing/cost enforcement: AWS documentation explicitly warns usage-plan quotas can be exceeded and must not gate spend — metering-based billing is the system of record, throttling is protection.
nginx-based gateway data planes: Google retired ESPv1 (nginx) for Envoy-based ESPv2 — the filter-chain/xDS model won.

Shared multi-tenant gateway fleets without engineered isolation: AWS's answer to noisy neighbors is shuffle-sharding the node assignment, not bigger fleets; flat shared fleets are the documented failure mode.

Hand-editing derived/federated schemas: AppSync Merged APIs use canonical-type directives + auto-merge instead of hand-merged GraphQL; Oyatie's own spec already bans hand-maintained GraphQL — hyperscaler practice confirms it.

Manual marketplace fulfillment: all four clouds made webhook/event-driven entitlement lifecycle + API-integrated metering a CERTIFICATION REQUIREMENT (Azure certification policies; AWS FTR) — human-in-the-loop fulfillment does not pass listing review.

Rigid per-endpoint fixed rate limits at developer-platform scale: Meta retired them (2016 page-level redesign) for rolling-window budget scoring per app/business entity with usage surfaced in response headers.

Blocking the gateway data plane on control-plane availability: 'fail static' is universal — a gateway that stops serving when config delivery degrades is considered defective (Azure self-hosted GW, Apigee Synchronizer design).

Lambda-authorizer-style out-of-process policy hops as the permanent design: AWS mitigates the added hop with aggressive decision caching; in-process evaluation is strictly better when you own the gateway binary.
oyatie_prescriptions: Contract SSOT (extends specs/api-contract-ssot-canonical.json / ADR-0358): steal Smithy's ARCHITECTURE — protocol-agnostic typed model + trait system + resource shapes + build tool with model-diff — not its syntax. The Rust contract crates are the model; buck2 rules run emitters producing OpenAPI 3.2, proto3, GraphQL SDL, axum server scaffolding, tonic bindings, and typed Rust/TS clients as content-addressed build outputs. Adopt TypeSpec's emitter-plugin pattern so each projection is an independent emitter crate, and Google's numbered-AIP + api-linter pattern as a CI lint gate (Oyatie design rules as numbered, machine-checkable lints). The planned api-contract-ssot-drift gate is exactly Smithy's model-diff + Azure's spec-repo gating — also publish generated models publicly à la aws/api-models-aws for agent/tool consumption.

Gateway: bespoke Rust (axum/tower data plane) but adopt the Envoy operating model wholesale — xDS-style dynamic config protocol from a Rust control-plane service, listener/filter-chain abstraction, and Azure APIM's four-stage policy pipeline (inbound/backend/outbound/on-error) attachable at global/product/API/operation scope as the policy authoring model. MANDATORY fail-static: persist last-known-good config to local volume; data plane never blocks on control plane (Azure self-hosted GW + Apigee Synchronizer precedent).

Gateway as PEP with Cedar IN-PROCESS: embed the cedar-policy crate directly in the gateway — AWS Verified Permissions + API Gateway proves Cedar-at-the-edge; Oyatie beats AWS's Lambda-authorizer hop because it owns the binary. Edge does TLS termination, token validation (JWT/OAuth client-credentials), coarse Cedar decision with TTL-cached (principal, action, resource) results; services re-evaluate fine-grained Cedar near data (BeyondProd defense-in-depth). Policy distribution rides the same xDS-style config channel.

Rate limiting/quota: implement Google Service Control's exact discipline in Rust — per-node local token buckets, check-result caching (~60s), batched usage reports, predictive quota prefetch, ≤1 global sync per (service, consumer, metric) per second; global reconciliation service backed by the bespoke distributed SQL store. Document quotas as best-effort protection (AWS honesty); billing truth comes only from metering records, transported over Pulsar.

Throttle hierarchy: codify AWS's documented evaluation order as the spec — per-key/per-operation (usage plan) → per-operation stage → per-tenant → per-cell platform limit. Separate SpikeArrest-class protection limits from Quota-class monetization limits (Apigee distinction). Shuffle-shard API keys/tenants across gateway nodes within each cell (Hyperplane precedent: shuffle-sharded multi-tenant packet processors) — this composes directly with Oyatie's decided cell + shuffle-sharding substrate.

Make 'API product' a first-class control-plane resource (cloud-control-plane-canonical.json): product = {operation set} × {rate, burst, quota period, metering dimensions} bound to subscriber/key resources — the convergent synthesis of AWS usage plans, APIM products, OCI usage-plan entitlements, Apigee API products. OCI's schema (usage plan → entitlements[] → {rate, quota, target deployments} + subscriber tokens) is the cleanest one to model directly in Rust types.

Marketplace: implement the canonical four-stage flow as single-concern Rust services per ADR-0132 (no bundling): (1) listing pipeline with automated certification gates (Azure certification-policy + AWS FTR model — integration tests ARE the listing review); (2) ResolveCustomer-style purchase-token exchange; (3) entitlement service with GetEntitlements pull + lifecycle events pushed on Pulsar topics (webhook adapter for external ISVs); (4) BatchMeterUsage-style metering ingestion — idempotent records keyed (customer, dimension, hour), 6-hour late window, retry-with-backoff contract, feeding the payout ledger in the bespoke distributed SQL store. Follow Google, not AWS: ONE metering substrate shared by first-party Oyatie services and marketplace ISVs.

Model private offers + channel from day one in the entitlement schema (AWS private offers/CPPO, Oracle MPPO, Azure private offers): entitlement → offer → {listing, pricing override, term, parties[]} so multi-party reseller deals are a data-model case, not a rewrite.

Developer portal as an explicit third plane (Azure's management/gateway/portal split): portal content — docs, try-it console, SDK downloads, key self-service, live usage — is GENERATED from the same contract SSOT, never hand-authored per API. Return quota/usage state in response headers on every call (Meta X-App-Usage pattern): trivial to implement in the owned gateway, best-in-class developer ergonomics.

GraphQL stays derived-only per the existing spec; for multi-team composition adopt AppSync Merged-API semantics (canonical-type conflict directives + auto-merge) enforced by the drift gate rather than hand-federated schemas — but since all three surfaces derive from one Rust source, Oyatie gets federation-by-construction that AWS had to bolt on.

Edge front door: anycast BGP + split TCP TLS termination at POPs (GFE/Front Door/CloudFront convergence; note Azure's 2026 anycast-DNS retreat — keep DNS unicast-capable); L4 layer as Katran-style XDP/eBPF forwarding with Maglev-class consistent hashing living in the owned Talos-style OS/kernel layer (Meta proves bespoke L4+L7 in an owned systems language is the durable position). L7 gateway fleet deploys per-cell; control plane regional; cells are the blast-radius and capacity unit for the gateway itself.

Auth surface: support both API keys (packaging/metering identity) and OAuth2 client-credentials (security identity) — all five separate these concerns; keys select the usage plan/product, tokens authenticate. Never overload one as the other (AWS/Azure/Apigee all converged on the dual model).

research.domain: Audit + Compliance + Governance + Data Residency substrate (audit event taxonomy, tamper-evidence, audit pipeline availability, compliance-as-code, residency enforcement, provider-access audit, purpose limitation, retention/legal hold, certification evidence automation)

per_company.approach: CloudTrail: management-events (control-plane, on by default via 90-day Event history) vs data-events (opt-in, paid) split; at-least-once delivery to S3 ('designed to support at least one delivery... could deliver the same event more than once' — consumers dedup on eventID), typical ~5-min delivery latency (not guaranteed; was documented 15 min until Mar 2023). Integrity validation: SHA-256 hash per log file + hourly digest files, each digest references prior digest's signature (hash chain), RSA-SHA256 signed with per-region key pairs, validated via `aws cloudtrail validate-logs`. CloudTrail Lake: immutable (read-only) event data stores in Apache ORC columnar format, Trino SQL queries, retention up to 3,653 days (10y extendable pricing) or 2,557 days (7y). AWS Config: configuration recorder + managed/custom rules (Lambda/Guard), conformance packs (YAML rule+remediation bundles) deployed org-wide via Organizations, auto-remediation via SSM automation documents, proactive (pre-provision) evaluation mode added later, compliance score per pack. Audit Manager: prebuilt SOC 2 (SSAE-18)/ISO/PCI frameworks; automated evidence collection from CloudTrail activity, Config snapshots, Security Hub checks, and scheduled API snapshots, transformed into audit-ready evidence per control. Artifact: on-demand provider attestations (SOC, ISO 27001/17/18, PCI, K-ISMS). S3 Object Lock: WORM with governance vs compliance mode (compliance mode immune to root) + legal hold (no expiry). Sovereign: AWS European Sovereign Cloud — €7.8B investment, first region Brandenburg (launched end-2025/Jan-2026 per press), physically separate infrastructure, EU-resident-only ops/support staff, independent EU-controlled parent company, dedicated EU SOC. K-ISMS: first global CSP certified (KISA), Seoul region with 144 services in scope, current cert valid Dec 2023–Dec 2026; also first K-ISMS-P. Cedar policy language: Rust implementation formally verified in Lean, differential random testing, sound+complete SMT encoding for policy analysis (arXiv 2403.04651), runs at cloud scale in Amazon Verified Permissions.

Cloud Audit Logs: four-stream taxonomy — Admin Activity (always written, cannot be disabled or excluded, free, 400-day retention in non-deletable _Required bucket), Data Access (opt-in per service, paid, DATA_READ/DATA_WRITE/ADMIN_READ classes, _Default bucket 30-day default configurable), System Event (free, Google-system-initiated changes), Policy Denied (security-policy denials logged by default). Canonical protoPayload schema (google.cloud.audit.AuditLog): authenticationInfo, authorizationInfo[], serviceName, methodName, resourceName, request/response — the cleanest published who-did-what-to-which-resource schema. Access Transparency: near-real-time logs of Google personnel accesses to customer data with justification (e.g., support case ref) — the trailblazing provider-access audit; Access Approval: Google admin access requires prior customer approval (fail-closed gate, notify via email/PubSub). Assured Workloads: per-regime control packages (FedRAMP Moderate/High, IL4, EU sovereignty) applied at folder scope; enforced via Organization Policy constraints (resource location restriction to allowed regions, service/API-endpoint allowlists), personnel controls (geo + background-check attributes, Assured Support), KMS key rings provisioned in-region, continuous monitoring dashboard for org-policy drift vs compliance posture. Org Policy: built-in constraints + custom constraints in CEL (max 1000 chars) evaluated at CREATE/UPDATE in the resource API path with ALLOW/DENY — preventive, admission-time. GCS Bucket Lock: retention policies lockable irreversibly (WORM) + object-level retention lock + retention holds. K-ISMS certified.

Activity Log: subscription-scope control-plane platform log (Resource Manager operations), 90-day free retention then deleted; longer retention requires diagnostic-settings routing to Log Analytics/Storage/Event Hubs (legacy storage-retention setting deprecated). Resource logs cover data plane, separately enabled. Azure Policy: JSON policy-as-code evaluated at ARM admission; effects: audit, deny (block create/update), append, modify, auditIfNotExists, deployIfNotExists (DINE — allows the deployment then deploys remediation ARM template after success, after configurable delay), denyAction; guest configuration extends compliance inside VMs (DINE-based, but DINE guest-config not assignable at management-group scope — AuditIfNotExists only); initiatives bundle policies; remediation tasks for existing resources. Purview Audit: unified audit log across Exchange/SharePoint/OneDrive/Teams/Entra capturing thousands of operation types; Audit (Standard) default retention raised 90→180 days (Oct 2023); Audit (Premium) custom retention policies up to 1 year, 10 years with add-on license; plus Purview data governance (catalog/classification) and eDiscovery legal holds. EU Data Boundary: the largest published residency engineering program — completed Feb 26, 2025 in three phases: Phase 1 Jan 2023 (customer data for M365/Dynamics/Power Platform/Azure stored+processed in EU/EFTA), Phase 2 Jan 2024 (pseudonymized personal data), Phase 3 Feb 2025 (professional-services/support data incl. logs and case notes); multi-year effort across hundreds of product teams and thousands of engineers; logical boundary across existing EU regions rather than a separate physical cloud. Immutable blob storage: time-based retention policies + legal hold (WORM until explicitly cleared), version-level immutability. Customer Lockbox provides approval workflow for Microsoft support access. K-ISMS offering documented.

OCI Audit: always-on, tenancy-wide recording of control-plane API calls (time, source, target, action) across all services; event envelope follows the CNCF CloudEvents standard (v0.1 spec) — the only hyperscaler that adopted an open envelope standard for audit events; payload carries identity, request, response, and stateChange (before/after) sections; retention configurable at tenancy level up to a 365-day maximum; feeds Events service, Service Connector Hub, and Logging Analytics for compliance analytics/enforcement. Sovereign: OCI EU Sovereign Cloud operational since 2023 (first mover — Frankfurt + Madrid regions, single AD each at launch), architected as isolated REALMS: physical separation (separate hardware, data halls/caging), logical separation (separate realm = separate identity/trust domain, no cross-realm dependencies), cryptographic separation; operated by EU-incorporated legal entities that own the hardware and data-center leases; physical+logical access and day-to-day operations restricted to EU-resident personnel of dedicated EU entities. The realm primitive (also behind Dedicated Region, Alloy, Isolated Region, Gov clouds) is OCI's distinctive sovereignty mechanism. Operator Access Control provides approval-gated provider access for Exadata/infrastructure. OCI Audit usable to drive governance enforcement actions per published sovereign-cloud architecture guide.

Privacy Aware Infrastructure (PAI) + Policy Zones: purpose limitation enforced INLINE via Information Flow Control rather than post-hoc audits. Data labeled with Governable Data Annotations (GDAs) — deliberately flat, hierarchy-free, human-readable labels (e.g., MESSAGING_DATA) at table/column/row/cell granularity in batch systems and request-parameter/variable granularity in function-based systems; derived data must carry equal-or-more-restrictive labels. Enforcement points: function-based systems (Hack/C++/Python web/middle-tier/backends via PrivacyLib at low-level data-access call sites), batch warehouse (UPM SQL parser intercepts Presto/Spark/Dataswarm queries into semantic trees of inputs/outputs/transformations), stream processing (XStream, multiple petabytes/hour, static analysis before event processing), and ML training control plane (checks workflow definitions, not rows). Services: Policy Evaluation Service (PES) for flow-control checks, Warehouse Permission Service (WPS) for final policy-aware access validation; cryptographically signed context tokens propagate purpose through compute engines. Published scale: tens of millions of data flows analyzed per day across hundreds of thousands of unique queries; access control for millions of datasets; trillions of user-consent checks per hour; hundreds of distinct policy requirements per flow. Rollout doctrine: logging mode first (detect, don't block), then enforcement mode (auto-block unremediated violations); reclassification mechanism stops label over-propagation when data is desensitized; 10x compute-efficiency work (simplified policy lattice, native context propagation, canonicalized annotations) was required for viability. Tooling: Policy Zone Manager (automated downstream-flow discovery, ML classifiers for asset identification, annotation-effect simulation, flow suspension for remediation), Dr. PZ (genAI remediation guidance). Published lessons: solve one end-to-end use case first; simple independent annotations are a must; physical data segregation per purpose rejected as cost-prohibitive vs annotation-based logical separation.

convergent_patterns: Two-tier audit taxonomy with asymmetric guarantees (all 5): control-plane/admin-activity events are always-on, non-disableable, and free/default (CloudTrail management events, GCP Admin Activity in non-deletable _Required bucket, Azure Activity Log, OCI Audit, Meta's always-on flow logging); data-plane/data-access events are opt-in, paid, and volume-managed (CloudTrail data events, GCP Data Access logs, Azure resource logs). The control-plane stream is treated as a platform invariant, not a customer feature.

Canonical who-did-what-to-which-resource event schema (all 5): every audit record carries authenticated principal (+ delegation chain), service + method/operation, canonical resource identifier, request parameters, response/status, source IP, and timestamps; GCP's AuditLog proto adds explicit authorizationInfo[] (which permission was checked, granted or denied); OCI proves CloudEvents works as the standard envelope for exactly this payload; OCI uniquely includes before/after stateChange.

Audit delivery is at-least-once / never-drop, with duplicates accepted over loss (AWS, GCP, OCI, Meta): CloudTrail explicitly documents at-least-once delivery with possible duplicate events (dedup on eventID downstream); GCP Admin Activity cannot be disabled, excluded, or deleted before 400 days; OCI Audit is always-on and non-optional; Meta enforces inline (blocking) only after logging-mode burn-in. Latency is explicitly NOT guaranteed (CloudTrail ~5-min typical, 'this time is not guaranteed') — the doctrine is durability over latency over throughput.

Tamper-evidence via cryptographic digest chains + WORM storage, not trusted databases (AWS, +WORM in GCP/Azure/OCI): CloudTrail computes SHA-256 per log file, hourly digest files each containing prior digest's signature (hash chain) signed RSA-SHA256 with per-region keys; audit lakes are immutable/read-only by construction (CloudTrail Lake ORC stores); all three big clouds ship WORM object retention with an un-revokable compliance mode plus a no-expiry legal-hold flag (S3 Object Lock, GCS Bucket Lock irreversible policy lock, Azure immutable blob).

Resource-compliance-as-code = declarative rules over a continuously-recorded resource-state inventory, with the preventive/detective/remediative triad (AWS, Azure, GCP): admission-time deny (Azure Policy deny at ARM, GCP org-policy CEL constraints at CREATE/UPDATE, AWS Config proactive mode), continuous detective evaluation against the configuration recorder, and declared auto-remediation (Azure DINE templates, AWS SSM automation docs); rules are packaged as versioned, org-deployable bundles (conformance packs, policy initiatives, Assured Workloads control packages) with a compliance score.

Residency enforced as location-constraint policy + sovereign realm + in-region personnel + local legal entity (AWS, GCP, Azure, OCI): org-level resource-location constraints restrict where resources can be created (GCP resourceLocations via Assured Workloads, Azure Policy location rules, sovereign-region allowlists); the high-assurance tier adds physically/logically isolated realms operated exclusively by in-region residents employed by locally-incorporated entities (OCI EU Sovereign realms 2023, AWS European Sovereign Cloud 2025/26 with EU parent company, Azure EU Data Boundary personnel+support phases); in-region KMS key residency is bundled with every residency package.

Provider-access audit + approval is now table stakes (GCP, Azure, OCI): GCP Access Transparency (near-real-time logs of provider personnel access with justification) + Access Approval (fail-closed customer pre-approval); Azure Customer Lockbox; OCI Operator Access Control; AWS competes via 'no operator access by design' (Nitro) plus sovereign-cloud staffing controls. A separate audit stream class for operator access is an industry-converged requirement.

Certification evidence is derived automatically from the audit + config planes, never collected manually (AWS explicit, GCP/Azure equivalent): AWS Audit Manager maps controls to evidence auto-pulled from CloudTrail, Config, Security Hub, and scheduled API snapshots, transformed into per-control audit-ready evidence; provider-side attestations distributed as self-serve artifacts (AWS Artifact, Azure Service Trust Portal, GCP Compliance Reports Manager); same machinery underwrites K-ISMS (KISA assessed AWS Seoul region with 144 services in scope).

Tiered retention: hot queryable audit lake (columnar + SQL: CloudTrail Lake Trino/ORC 7–10y options; Purview Premium up to 10y; GCP 400-day _Required + BigQuery sinks) over WORM archive, with legal hold as an indefinite override orthogonal to retention periods (all of S3/GCS/Azure blob).
divergences: Preventive vs detective center of gravity: Azure Policy's primary mode is admission-time deny inside ARM; GCP org policy is likewise preventive in the API path (CEL at CREATE/UPDATE); AWS Config grew up detective (record-then-evaluate, remediate after) and only later added proactive mode — AWS splits prevention across SCPs/IAM instead. No one regrets prevention; AWS's late addition signals detective-only is insufficient.

Sovereign-cloud architecture strategy: Microsoft engineered a LOGICAL boundary across its existing EU regions (EU Data Boundary — 3 phases, 2023–2025, hundreds of teams re-plumbing data flows service by service); AWS and Oracle built PHYSICALLY separate realms with separate legal entities and staff (Oracle shipped 2023, AWS end-2025); Google sells folder-scoped control packages (Assured Workloads) on shared infrastructure plus partner-operated sovereign clouds. Trade: logical boundary preserves service parity but costs years of retrofit; separate realms launch clean but with reduced service catalogs.

No convergence on policy language: Azure uses a JSON effects DSL, GCP uses CEL, AWS uses Guard/Lambda for config rules but built Cedar (formally verified, analyzable) for application authorization, Meta uses flat annotations + IFC. Only OCI adopted an open standard (CloudEvents) and only for the audit envelope, not policy.

Purpose-limitation depth: Meta enforces purpose binding INSIDE compute engines (SQL parsing, signed context tokens, trillions of consent checks/hour) — no public cloud offers customer-facing information-flow control; clouds stop at resource-level and access-level policy. This is the largest capability gap between internal-platform and public-cloud governance.

Default control-plane audit retention varies 4x: 90 days (CloudTrail Event history, Azure Activity Log) vs 180 days (Purview Audit Standard, raised from 90 post-Storm-0558) vs 365 days (OCI max) vs 400 days (GCP _Required, non-deletable). Microsoft's raise after the 2023 nation-state incident shows 90 days is now considered inadequate.

Provider-access control posture: Google = fail-closed pre-approval (Access Approval); Microsoft/Oracle = scoped approval workflows (Lockbox, Operator Access Control); AWS = architectural elimination of operator access (Nitro attestations) rather than approval workflow — two philosophies: 'audit + approve the human' vs 'remove the human'.
anti_patterns: Best-effort audit delivery / dropping audit events under load — universally rejected; every provider guarantees always-written (GCP/OCI) or at-least-once-with-duplicates (CloudTrail), and trades latency (unguaranteed ~5 min) for durability, never the reverse.

Mutable or DB-trusted audit stores — retired in favor of read-only-by-construction lakes (CloudTrail Lake), signed digest chains, and WORM object storage; audit integrity never rests on database ACLs alone.

Post-hoc audits / periodic reviews as the primary privacy control — Meta explicitly moved away from audit-after-the-fact to inline runtime IFC enforcement (Policy Zones) because audits don't scale to millions of data flows.
Physical data segregation per purpose — Meta evaluated and rejected it as cost-prohibitive; annotation-based logical separation 'at relatively low compute cost' won.

Hierarchical/complex label taxonomies and policy lattices — Meta retired these for flat, hierarchy-free, independent human-readable GDA labels after propagation conflicts and 10x-too-expensive evaluation; 'simplified and independent annotations are a must'.
Manual evidence collection (screenshots, spreadsheets) for certifications — replaced by automated evidence pipelines off the audit/config planes (Audit Manager pattern).

Residency as a retrofit — Microsoft's EU Data Boundary consumed 3+ years and thousands of engineers re-plumbing existing services; the industry lesson is data location must be a first-class property of every service from day one.

90-day default audit retention — Microsoft raised Purview default to 180 days after the 2023 Storm-0558 incident exposed customers who couldn't investigate; GCP's 400-day non-deletable bucket is the high bar.

Remediation-only enforcement — Azure DINE allows non-compliant deployment then fixes it after a delay, and guest-config DINE can't even be assigned at management groups; no provider relies on auto-remediation without an admission-time deny tier.
Azure's legacy Activity Log storage-retention setting — deprecated in favor of explicit diagnostic-settings routing; per-store retention knobs lose to centralized routing + bucket policies.
oyatie_prescriptions: Canonical audit event = CloudEvents 1.0 envelope (OCI precedent) + GCP AuditLog-shaped payload, as a serde-typed struct in a shared libs/ crate: {authentication_info (principal + delegation chain), authorization_info[] (each Cedar permission checked + decision), service, method, canonical resource ID (cell+region embedded), request_params, response_status, state_change {before,after} (OCI precedent), event_class}. Emit from a tower/axum middleware layer so every {oya,cloud}/<service> gets correct audit emission for free — no per-service hand-rolling.

Five-stream taxonomy day one with asymmetric guarantees: admin_activity (always-on, non-disableable, free-quota, >=400-day retention — GCP bar, never 90), data_access (opt-in per service, READ/WRITE/ADMIN_READ classes, sampling controls), system_event, policy_denied (every Cedar deny IS an audit event — GCP precedent), provider_access (see below). Control-plane audit is a platform invariant, not a feature flag.

Harden /Users/jasonlee/Developer/oyatie/evidence/audit-chain.jsonl into a CloudTrail-grade digest chain: SHA-256 per record batch + periodic digest records containing all batch hashes plus the PREVIOUS digest's signature (chain), Ed25519-signed with per-cell keys; ship a `verify` subcommand replicating `aws cloudtrail validate-logs` semantics (detect modify/delete/forge). Anchor digests in the W5 bespoke CAS object store — content addressing gives tamper evidence for free — and implement Object-Lock-class WORM there: governance mode, compliance mode (immune to all principals including root), and legal hold (no-expiry flag orthogonal to retention).

Audit pipeline doctrine: at-least-once over Pulsar (launch-primary) with UUIDv7 event IDs for downstream dedup; producers NEVER block the serving path and NEVER drop — backpressure goes to a local durable WAL spool per node, with alerting on spool depth; budget audit-ingest availability above serving SLO and author its OpenSLO files first (per ADR-0130 this is mandatory pre-dev-promotion anyway). Accept duplicates, never loss; document latency as typical-not-guaranteed (CloudTrail doctrine).

Subsume Config/Azure-Policy/org-policy with Cedar (it is strictly better-suited than all three incumbents' DSLs: formally verified in Lean, Rust-native, SMT-analyzable so packs can be proven non-overlapping/non-regressing on refactor): (a) preventive tier — evaluate Cedar against every resource CREATE/UPDATE at the API gateway, GCP-org-policy style, deny before mutate; (b) detective tier — Config-recorder pattern: persist every resource-state transition into the bespoke distributed-SQL inventory and continuously re-evaluate Cedar policy sets against it; (c) remediative tier — declared, themselves-audited remediation actions. Package rule sets as versioned 'conformance packs' in the buck2 monorepo, shipped via the content-addressed delivery fabric, with per-pack compliance scores (AWS pattern).

Residency = Assured-Workloads-style control packages, KR pack day one: a pack bundles Cedar location constraints (pin resource creation to KR cells), service/API allowlist, in-region KMS key residency, and personnel/agent access constraints; enforce at admission, continuously monitor drift against the pack (Assured Workloads monitoring pattern). Make region/realm/cell a first-class, immutable field of every resource ID NOW — Microsoft's 3-year, thousands-of-engineers EU Data Boundary retrofit is the cautionary tale; cells + shuffle-sharding are the natural realm boundary (OCI realm model: separate trust domains, no cross-realm dependencies).

Implement Access Transparency + Access Approval analogs day one — this is doubly critical for Oyatie because OPERATORS ARE AGENTS: every operator/agent access to customer data emits a provider_access event with justification (ticket/IP reference), and sensitive-data access requires customer or policy pre-approval, fail-closed (GCP precedent, the trailblazing feature). This is a marketable differentiator AWS still lacks in standard regions.

Purpose limitation for the messenger/mail personal-professional split = adopt Meta Policy Zones methodology wholesale, reimplemented Rust-native: flat, hierarchy-free purpose annotations (GDA-style, e.g., PERSONAL_MSG_DATA) attached at source (logging/SDK layer), propagated as cryptographically signed context tokens through Pulsar topics and into the distributed-SQL/batch layers; enforce IFC in the shared Rust data-access crate at low-level call sites (PrivacyLib pattern) with PES/WPS-analog services; derived data carries equal-or-stricter labels; include a reclassification mechanism to stop over-propagation. Rollout per Meta's published lessons: logging mode first, enforcement second; solve the personal/professional split as the ONE end-to-end use case before generalizing; keep annotations simple and independent.

Evidence automation (Audit-Manager pattern) targeting SOC 2, ISO 27001, and K-ISMS/K-ISMS-P (KISA-assessed — AWS Seoul precedent covered infra ops with 144 services in scope; KR pack + this machinery is the certification path): map each control to queries over the audit chain + resource-compliance inventory; auto-collect evidence snapshots on schedules; store evidence WORM under the digest chain; generate auditor-facing artifact bundles (Artifact analog) from the same store. Never manual screenshots.

Retention machinery: tiered — hot queryable audit lake (columnar Parquet/ORC in the CAS store, SQL via the bespoke distributed-SQL engine or embedded DataFusion; CloudTrail Lake precedent: immutable event data stores, 7-and-10-year retention tiers) over WORM cold archive; legal hold as an indefinite, explicitly-cleared override flag on CAS objects (uniform S3/GCS/Azure semantics); retention policies lockable-irreversible for the compliance tier (GCS Bucket Lock precedent).

decision_matrix.decision: Build oya-kms as the AWS-domain-model clone: per-cell sealing 'domain' root -> versioned per-tenant KEKs persisted ONLY as wrapped key-tokens -> on-demand per-object DEKs returned wrapped+plaintext over mTLS, never persisted. KEK plaintext lives ONLY inside a dedicated zeroize+mlock crypto-enclave process; one-way-door enforced in the type system (no trait/API/Debug path returns root/KEK plaintext). Transitional wrap/custody layer = the existing OpenBao adapter (cloud-secrets IP-006) + a small PKCS#11 FIPS-140-3-L3 device pair for root sealing; cutover to a bespoke Azure-Managed-HSM-pattern Rust enclave-replicated key service (3 replicas across racks/AZs, attested mTLS pinned to the Oyatie code-signing key, SEV-SNP/TPM measured-boot). Secrets distribution = identity not secrets: bespoke Rust internal CA mints SPIFFE-style mTLS workload certs at pod admission (fetch-fail = deploy-fail), KDF(ica_secret, identity, epoch) derives session/cache keys (zero cross-cell sync), DB/Pulsar creds are leased dynamic secrets behind OpenBao API compat. Key authz IS Cedar (key policies = Cedar policies, decision-id embedded in audit). cloud-kms/cloud-secrets PRD/ARCH docs already encode this; wire the running Rust now.
decision_matrix.hyperscaler_precedent: AWS KMS HBK/EKT + CDK domain model, 'no mechanism to export plaintext keys', per-command quorum-signed domain mutations; Azure Managed HSM SGX attested-TLS + Shamir security-domain; Google root-key-in-RAM distributor + Titan measured-boot sealed credentials; Meta KDF-derived STEKs + container-setup cert issuance; HashiCorp/OpenBao barrier + Shamir unseal + transit auto-unseal + dynamic-secret leases.
decision_matrix.rationale: KMS outage = everything-outage, so the one-way-door + static-stability discipline is the highest-stakes item and must be in the type system from commit one. ADR-0510 doctrine: OpenBao+PKCS#11 is a PROVEN transitional impl behind the stable oya-kms Rust interface; the bespoke enclave service is the cutover-gated destination — adopting OpenBao now buys correct envelope+lease semantics immediately while the enclave matures, and the Cedar-as-key-authz unification avoids inventing a second authz language alongside the already-decided policy engine.

decision_matrix.decision: DNS is W0-critical: bespoke Rust authoritative server (hickory-dns as reference impl behind stable interface), Route-53 Infima shuffle-shard-of-4-from-2048-virtual-NS ported to Rust, anycast per cell, serving EXCLUSIVELY from complete signed zone snapshots pulled from the CAS delivery fabric — must run with control plane dead. Hard code invariant: no automation may ever emit an empty/below-floor record set, and DNS never withdraws its own reachability on backend health (codifies AWS-Oct-2025 + Meta-Oct-2021 lessons). L4 = Rust Katran-equivalent (aya eBPF/XDP, Maglev hashing, local-only conn table, DSR via IPIP/GUE, BGP/ECMP VIPs, co-located on workload nodes). L7 = Rust GFE-equivalent on hyper/tower+rustls (h2/h3, split-TCP, GSLB cell selection). Mesh = library not sidecar (tower middleware: discovery, locality LB, retries/hedging, in-process Cedar). East-west = ALTS-model workload-identity mTLS on by default. Control/data split is a repo rule: each cloud/cloud-network* ships a config-compiler (publishes CAS snapshots) + a dataplane that pulls/verifies/atomic-swaps and FAILS STATIC on staleness; constant-work fixed-cadence full-snapshot fetch, never event-driven deltas.
decision_matrix.hyperscaler_precedent: AWS Route 53 (100% data-plane SLA, 2048 virtual NS, single-region control plane), Hyperplane constant-work DynamoDB->S3 config push, static-stability/zonal-shift; Google Maglev+GFE two-tier, Andromeda hoverboard, Orion fail-static + out-of-band control + DAG capability check, ALTS->PSP; Meta Katran XDP + ServiceRouter 99%-library mesh; Azure AccelNet/VFP, Front Door anycast->unicast migration.
decision_matrix.rationale: All five companies' first-decade network investments are L4-LB + authoritative-DNS + L7-proxy + mesh-library — this is the proven, non-speculative shape and the lowest-risk path to FD-001 multi-tenant serving. The fail-static + minimum-viable-answer-floor invariants are the two most expensive lessons hyperscalers published (both caused multi-hour outages) and cost nothing to encode now. Sidecars are a retired pattern at hyperscale (Meta quantified hundreds-of-thousands-of-machines saved; Istio itself retreated to ambient), and owning the binary makes in-process Cedar strictly better than an authz hop.

decision_matrix.decision: Keep the ratified multi-Raft leader-per-range anchor. Transitional impl behind the stable oya-data Rust SQL interface = PROVEN substrate (CockroachDB/TiKV-class semantics, or a managed Spanner-shaped store) per ADR-0510; bespoke Rust distributed-SQL (Pebble-class LSM + dedicated multi-Raft log store + HLC behind a TrueTime-shaped ClockSource trait returning [earliest,latest]) is the W5 cutover-gated destination. Range = single unit of consensus/placement/split/repair/CDC-sharding. Clock launches on NTP-grade sync with CRDB-style uncertainty restarts (max-offset ~250-500ms); the SAME trait later accepts PTP/owned-time for commit-wait external consistency without protocol rewrite. F1 online async schema change (delete-only->write-only->backfill->public) from the first DDL; blocking DDL = governance-gate violation. CDC as a Spanner-style DDL schema object, change records written transactionally, stream shards split with ranges, delivered over Pulsar. Continuous log archival to the CAS object store = per-second PITR / 35-day window as a pipeline property. Placement driver = separate consensus-backed Rust service (TiKV-PD analog); ranges never cross cells; routing tier shuffle-sharded per tenant and constant-work (MemDS lesson). Tenant isolation = per-range + per-router token buckets + proactive Global Admission Control + RU-style normalized cost unit; split-for-heat automatic. Witness/log-only replica roles supported from the start.
decision_matrix.hyperscaler_precedent: Spanner (Paxos-per-split, TrueTime, F1 schema change, change streams, online SSTable->Ressi engine swap); DynamoDB (multi-Paxos leader-per-partition, GAC, MemDS constant-work, split-for-heat, per-second PITR); CockroachDB/TiKV (Raft-per-range, HLC, Pebble clean-room engine, Raft-Engine log store); Aurora (log-is-the-database, 4/6 quorum, S3 archival).
decision_matrix.rationale: Multi-Raft leader-per-range is the universal convergence endpoint — every player that started leaderless (Dynamo 2007) or single-leader migrated here, so the anchor is de-risked. ADR-0510 mandates a proven substrate behind the owned interface until the bespoke engine clears its cutover triggers; building the SQL layer (placement driver, RU admission, CDC, F1 DDL, clock trait) on a proven storage engine first means FD-001 tenancy gets a real database NOW while the bespoke LSM matures, and Spanner's online engine swap proves the trait-behind-versioned-format escape hatch works at >2B QPS.

decision_matrix.decision: W5 CAS = four planes (stateless axum front-end / metadata-index / append-only chunk-data / background fleet-mgmt), each a single-concern ADR-0132 service. Metadata stored in the oya-data distributed-SQL with Tectonic's three independent keyspaces (Name/Object/Block); explicit bootstrap ADR for the recursion (small static-config seed instance). Strong read-after-write from the first commit (designed-in, never retrofit) -> unlocks conditional PUT. Durability = sealed immutable extents: 3x synchronous chain replication for ack (reconcile via minimum-commit-length), seal, then background LRC(12,2,2)=1.29x across >=3 fault domains; never inline EC on the hot path. Content addressing is Oyatie's legitimate divergence: chunk IDs = BLAKE3 (serves buck2 delivery fabric + integrity) PLUS an S3-style full-object checksum composing across multipart, validated end-to-end; dedup strictly per-tenant/per-cell (never cross-tenant); refcount GC in metadata plane only. Continuous-verification plane before GA (scrubbers re-checksum, redundancy-loss auto-repair <30min OCI bar, AWS-style human durability reviews wired into governance). Adopt ShardStore methodology literally: ~40k-LOC Rust node validated by executable reference model + proptest/stateright on every commit in oya-ci (spec ~10-15% of code). Chunk store stays dumb/flat so it later serves Pulsar tiered storage + DB backups + buck2 artifacts. Until GA, the transitional CAS impl behind the stable oya-storage interface is a proven object store (S3-compatible MinIO-class self-hosted), cutover-gated to the bespoke CAS.
decision_matrix.hyperscaler_precedent: S3 ShardStore (40k-line Rust node + lightweight formal methods, 16 bugs caught), strong-consistency witness + model-checking, CRC64NVME default checksums, decorrelation placement; Azure WAS stamps + sealed extents + LRC(12,2,2) 1.29x; Google Colossus metadata-in-Bigtable recursion; Meta Tectonic ZippyDB 3-keyspace metadata + flat chunk store + hedged RS(9,6) + TrafficClass; OCI <30min disk recovery + checksum self-heal.
decision_matrix.rationale: The CAS is the universal endgame substrate under every other stateful system (DB backups, Pulsar tiered storage, snapshots, build artifacts) so its correctness compounds — ShardStore is the direct published proof that bespoke-Rust 11-nines storage with lightweight formal methods is tractable for a small team, perfectly matching founder doctrine. ADR-0510: a proven S3-compatible store behind the owned interface lets FD-001 and the delivery fabric run immediately; the bespoke CAS is cutover-gated. Per-tenant-only dedup avoids the cross-tenant oracle/correlated-loss blast radius that is precisely why no hyperscaler ships public content-addressing.

decision_matrix.decision: One shared fleet, never per-team clusters (reject in ADR now — quantified 20-30% capacity tax). Cells of 5-10k nodes on k8s+Cluster-API; Twine-style 'entitlement' Rust service carves fungible quota per product lane. Isolation ladder as Cedar-enforced admission policy: Tier 0 first-party Rust = hardened runc/containerd; Tier 1 tenant-influenced code (SaaS plugins/queries/functions) = Firecracker microVM per tenant workload (adopt-and-fork the proven Apache-2.0 Rust artifact via a bespoke Rust runtime shim — the rare 'reimplement = adopt the proven Rust' case); Tier 2 stateful data planes = dedicated bare-metal cells (OCI predictability + physical trust boundary). Never shared-kernel across a tenant boundary. Talos-style zero-SSH dm-verity A/B-flip OS, no shell in image, Twine host-profiles applied on re-entitlement. Borg economic model: 4 priority bands, quota priced by band, reclamation runs batch (buck2 CI + analytics) on prod slack, prod-never-preempts-prod, compressible throttle / non-compressible kill. Unify delivery: ONE content-addressed substrate (the CAS) serves buck2 artifacts + OCI images + microVM snapshots (Lambda 512KiB convergent-encrypted chunk model, L1 worker + L2 cell erasure-coded cache). Cold-start = snapshot-restore over boot (SnapStart 100-200ms) + clean-page sharing + small warm pools, recycle long-lived microVMs on a timer. Allocator (Rust, per cell) = Protean policy/mechanism split + Borg best-fit/spread hybrid + best-of-k, 85-90% packing KPI on the SLO substrate.
decision_matrix.hyperscaler_precedent: Google Borg (priced-quota bands, ~20% reclaimed slack, prod-no-preempt) + Autopilot + gVisor; AWS Firecracker (Rust microVM, <125ms boot) + Lambda content-addressed loading + SnapStart + Nitro no-operator-access + Bottlerocket; Meta Twine (1M-machine single plane, entitlements, host-profiles, small-machines 18%/17%); Azure Protean (85-90% util) + Resource Central; OCI bare-metal-first off-box.
decision_matrix.rationale: Per-team clusters and stranded capacity are the named enemy at every hyperscaler; the shared-fleet + priced-priority-quota model is the single highest-ROI utilization lever and gives the dogfood an internal spot market for free. The isolation ladder's floor (never shared-kernel for tenant code) and ceiling (hardware root of trust) are unanimous; Firecracker is the one place founder doctrine's 'reimplement Rust-native' correctly means adopt-the-proven-Rust-artifact because it already IS production-proven Rust. Collapsing three delivery systems onto the CAS is the proven path to 50ms cold starts and removes a whole class of substrate.

decision_matrix.decision: oya-metering = single-concern axum batch-ingest -> Pulsar (never-lose class) -> idempotent sink in oya-data, dedup key (tenant_id, resource_id, dimension, usage_hour_utc) unique index + client idempotency_key, Azure-style 409 echo on duplicate. FOCUS 1.2 as the INTERNAL canonical schema day one (tenant_id + cell_id first-class tags). Three-clock doctrine: measure per-second (60s min), rate hourly (universal window), invoice monthly; 6-hour lateness window with explicit Expired rejection. Versioned immutable price book in oya-data (SKU = service+usage_type+operation, identifiers immutable forever); rating = pure deterministic fn (usage x price_book_version) -> append-only identified line items -> Billing-Conductor-class pro-forma re-rating + internal chargeback from one engine. Append-only double-entry subledger NOW with debits=credits enforced transactionally per journal entry (per-tenant journal ranges), Stripe-Ledger balance-state-machine verification, every journal mutation archived to CAS (FLASH S3 pattern, SOX/K-GAAP grade). Rev-rec (ASC 606/IFRS 15) models performance obligations as a read of the subledger. Tax = bespoke-Rust SEAM not content engine: TaxCalculator trait (jurisdiction resolution + versioned rate tables + invoice-finalization invocation + threshold monitoring), KR-VAT native + EU non-Union-OSS providers day one, Avalara/Stripe-Tax adapter slot behind the same trait (tax CONTENT is the one thing never reimplemented). Quota enforces / billing observes — hard boundary; budgets are alerts + optional auto-suspend. Dogfood: every oya/*+cloud/* service gets a billing account through the SAME pipeline from W1.
decision_matrix.hyperscaler_precedent: AWS CUR2.0/Marketplace MeterUsage (6h window, hourly dedup) + Savings-Plans greedy allocation + Billing Conductor re-rating + FLASH ledger (Oracle->DynamoDB+S3); Google BigQuery export + CUD proportional attribution + Borg priced-quota; Azure Marketplace metering (one-event-per-resource-per-dim-per-hour, 409, reconStatus) + commerce rev-rec; OCI Universal Credits; Meta RAS RRU + Flux + Global Reservations; Stripe Ledger/Tax/Rev-Rec; FOCUS 1.2.
decision_matrix.rationale: Metering is a pipeline (collect->idempotent dedup->window->deterministic rate->invoice) not a query, and the HOUR is the universal rating window even at per-second measurement — getting the three clocks and the immutable price-book/line-item discipline right up front is what makes invoice-close and SOX audit possible. FOCUS is the converged external schema all four clouds settled on; adopting it internally avoids the acknowledged-legacy bespoke-then-map cost. Tax content is the explicit never-reimplement carve-out behind a bespoke seam — KR-VAT + EU-OSS native covers FD-001's KR launch + EU residency, with the Avalara slot preserving the door.

decision_matrix.decision: Pulsar is VALIDATED as launch-primary (transitional impl behind a thin owned Rust client crate per ADR-0510). Ship the convergent trichotomy as THREE single-concern axum surfaces over ONE Pulsar substrate (ADR-0132 no-grouping): oya-queue (Shared/Key_Shared lease + visibility-timeout + retry-letter/DLQ + redrive), oya-stream (partitioned, cursor/seek replay, tiered storage), oya-bus (rules routing + push, CloudEvents 1.0 envelope). Tenant-keyed partitioning: ordering key = tenant_id[:aggregate_id]; one namespace per tenant tier/cell; shuffle-shard across broker+bookie cells; Cedar authz at the axum surface over Pulsar native tenant auth. Exactly-once doctrine in the API contract SSOT: transport is at-least-once PERIOD; cross-service correctness = transactional outbox in oya-data (same Raft-group commit) + idempotent consumer/inbox dedup + publish dedup tokens (5-min window); Pulsar transactions reserved for consume-transform-produce inside Pulsar only; never promise end-to-end EO in any public contract. Two explicit loss classes (never-lose: billing/audit/outbox; best-effort: telemetry). CAS wired as the Pulsar tiered-storage offloader (sealed immutable BookKeeper segments are content-addressed by nature). Schema registry server-side-enforced, BACKWARD_TRANSITIVE default (replay-heavy), AsyncAPI docs in the monorepo as cloud-ci admission gates. Bespoke-Rust W5 destination = stateless broker + BookKeeper-class segment store + embedded multi-Raft metadata (NO external coordinator, reuse oya-data multi-Raft) + tiered offload to CAS, cutover-gated.
decision_matrix.hyperscaler_precedent: Pulsar at Yahoo (100B msg/day, 1.4M topics, <5ms) + Tencent Midas billing (tens-of-billions txns/day, 99.999%); AWS SQS/Kinesis/EventBridge trichotomy + outbox doctrine; Azure Service Bus/Event Hubs/Event Grid events-vs-messages split; Meta Scribe (best-effort) + FOQS; Google Pub/Sub unified + Pub/Sub-Lite deprecation (kills the partitioned-lite tier); Kafka KRaft (ZooKeeper removal) + Oxia direction.
decision_matrix.rationale: Pulsar's tenant->namespace->topic hierarchy, namespace quotas, bookie-affinity, broker-isolation, and stateless-broker rebalancing are exactly the in-broker multi-tenant isolation Kafka lacks — and the Tencent Midas billing case is a direct existence proof for Oyatie's events-as-billing architecture on this exact substrate. The trichotomy is the convergent product taxonomy; serving it as three modes of one substrate (Pulsar + Google Pub/Sub both prove single-substrate works) honors ADR-0132 without running three broker fleets. Exactly-once-is-a-lie + outbox is the universal cross-system ground truth — encoding it in the contract SSOT prevents the most common distributed-systems correctness failure.
