Gateway = bespoke Rust (axum/tower) adopting the Envoy operating model (xDS-style dynamic config from a Rust control plane, filter-chain abstraction, APIM four-stage policy pipeline); MANDATORY fail-static (persist last-known-good to local volume, never block on control plane). Gateway as PEP with Cedar IN-PROCESS (cedar-policy crate embedded — beats AWS's Lambda-authorizer hop because we own the binary), TTL-cached decisions, fine-grained re-check near data. Rate limiting = Google Service Control discipline in Rust (local token buckets, ~60s check cache, batched reports, <=1 global sync/sec per (service,consumer,metric)); quotas documented best-effort, billing truth only from metering. 'API product' = first-class control-plane resource (OCI usage-plan->entitlements->{rate,quota,targets}+subscriber model). Marketplace = canonical four-stage flow as single-concern services (certified-listing-as-integration-test, ResolveCustomer token exchange, entitlement service with pull + Pulsar lifecycle events, BatchMeterUsage-shape ingestion feeding the payout ledger); ONE metering substrate shared first-party + ISV (Google not AWS); private/multi-party offers in the entitlement schema day one. Developer portal = explicit third plane, generated from the contract SSOT; X-App-Usage-style usage headers on every response.
decision_matrix.hyperscaler_precedent: AWS Smithy + api-models-aws + Hyperplane shuffle-sharding + Verified-Permissions-Cedar-at-edge + Marketplace MeterUsage/Entitlement; Google ESPv2/Envoy + Service Control (Check/AllocateQuota/Report) + AIPs + api-linter + IAP BeyondCorp + Procurement API on the same metering plane; Azure APIM three-plane + self-hosted-gateway fail-static + TypeSpec + SaaS Fulfillment v2; Meta GraphQL + budget-scored rate limits + App Review; OCI usage-plan entitlements + MPPO; Envoy as convergent open proxy.
decision_matrix.rationale: All three public clouds open-sourced their IDL and converged on the same doctrine: typed model is source, OpenAPI/GraphQL/proto are emitted projections, a linter+diff gate enforces design rules and backward compat — this is exactly the api-contract-ssot-drift gate already planned, so adopting Smithy's architecture (not syntax) over the Rust contract crates gives federation-by-construction. In-process Cedar at an owned gateway is strictly better than the Lambda-authorizer hop AWS is stuck with. Sharing ONE metering substrate across first-party and marketplace (Google's choice) collapses a whole service and makes dogfood chargeback and ISV payout the same code path.

decision_matrix.decision: Canonical audit event = CloudEvents 1.0 envelope (OCI precedent) + GCP-AuditLog-shaped payload as a serde struct in a shared libs/ crate {authentication_info incl. delegation chain, authorization_info[] (each Cedar permission + decision), service, method, canonical resource ID with cell+region embedded, request_params, response_status, state_change{before,after}, event_class}; emitted from tower/axum middleware so every service gets it free. Five-stream taxonomy with asymmetric guarantees: admin_activity (always-on, non-disableable, >=400-day retention — GCP bar, never 90), data_access (opt-in classes), system_event, policy_denied (every Cedar deny IS an audit event), provider_access (operators ARE agents -> every agent access to customer data emits justification + sensitive access needs fail-closed pre-approval; Access-Transparency+Access-Approval analog day one — a differentiator AWS standard regions lack). Harden the existing evidence/audit-chain.jsonl into a CloudTrail-grade digest chain: SHA-256 per batch + periodic digest referencing prior digest signature, Ed25519 per-cell keys, verify subcommand; anchor digests in CAS (content addressing = tamper evidence) with Object-Lock-class WORM (governance/compliance/legal-hold). Audit pipeline at-least-once over Pulsar, UUIDv7 IDs, never block serving / never drop (local durable WAL spool + backpressure alert), latency typical-not-guaranteed; audit-ingest SLO above serving SLO, authored first. Subsume Config/Azure-Policy/org-policy with Cedar (formally verified in Lean, SMT-analyzable so packs prove non-overlapping on refactor): preventive (Cedar at every CREATE/UPDATE, deny-before-mutate) + detective (resource-state transitions into oya-data inventory, continuous re-eval) + remediative (declared, self-audited); packs = versioned conformance bundles in the monorepo with compliance scores. Residency = Assured-Workloads-style control packs, KR pack day one (Cedar location constraints + service allowlist + in-region KMS + agent-access constraints, continuous drift monitoring); region/realm/cell immutable in every resource ID NOW (Microsoft's 3-year EU-Data-Boundary retrofit is the cautionary tale). Purpose limitation for messenger/mail personal-professional split = Meta Policy-Zones methodology Rust-native (flat hierarchy-free GDA labels at source, signed context tokens through Pulsar+oya-data, IFC enforced in the shared data-access crate, logging-mode-first then enforce). Evidence automation (Audit-Manager pattern) targeting SOC2/ISO27001/K-ISMS-P.
decision_matrix.hyperscaler_precedent: AWS CloudTrail digest-chain + Lake + Config conformance packs + Audit Manager + Cedar (Lean-verified) + S3 Object Lock + K-ISMS-first + European Sovereign Cloud; Google four-stream Cloud Audit Logs + Access Transparency/Approval + Assured Workloads + org-policy CEL; Azure EU Data Boundary (3-phase 3-year) + Purview 180-day + immutable blob + Customer Lockbox; OCI CloudEvents audit envelope + sovereign realms; Meta PAI/Policy-Zones IFC (flat GDAs, signed context tokens, logging-then-enforce).
decision_matrix.rationale: The control-plane audit stream is treated as a platform invariant (always-on, never-drop, durability-over-latency) at all five — emitting it from middleware over an at-least-once Pulsar pipeline into a CloudTrail-grade digest chain anchored in CAS gives tamper evidence and the certification path (K-ISMS-P for KR launch) cheaply. Cedar is strictly better-suited than all three incumbents' policy DSLs (Lean-verified, Rust-native, SMT-analyzable) so it subsumes Config/Azure-Policy/org-policy into one engine. Two Oyatie-specific amplifiers: operators are agents (so provider-access audit + fail-closed approval is doubly critical and a marketable differentiator), and the messenger/mail personal-professional split is a LIVE FD-001 purpose-limitation requirement that Meta's Policy-Zones is the only proven model for. Region/realm immutable in resource IDs from day one is the single cheapest insurance against Microsoft's thousands-of-engineers residency retrofit.

substrate_dependency_order: LAYER -1 (physical/OS, Wave-1-owned, assumed present): cloud-os/cloud-kernel Talos-style zero-SSH dm-verity OS + cloud-k8s (k8s + Cluster API) + cloud-cell/cell-lifecycle/cell-rebalancer cell substrate + cloud-iac OpenTofu fabric intent + cloud-observability (ADR-0130 SLO substrate). FD-001 FULL-DEPTH SLICE: one k8s cluster per cell, >=3 cells across fault domains, zonal-shift API, shuffle-shard tenant assignment live. W5-GATED: SDN WAN/TE (B4/EBB-class) + bespoke switch OS (SONiC/FBOSS-class) — only when Oyatie owns physical fabric; until then encode fabric intent in OpenTofu and keep the Orion intent model as the API boundary so hardware ownership is a backend swap.

LAYER 0 ROOT OF TRUST (must exist before any decryptable substrate): the oya-kms root ceremony — Shamir M-of-N offline root split across hardware tokens held by independent officers, recovery material in two geographically separate safes under dual-control. FD-001 FULL-DEPTH SLICE: OpenBao auto-unseal (proven transitional impl, ADR-0510) + PKCS#11 to a small FIPS-140-3-L3 device pair for root sealing; KMS's own storage is a minimal LOCAL Raft group (NOT oya-data) so it does not depend on the substrate it must decrypt; root key lives only in RAM across a peer-distributor set (Google distributor pattern) with safes as last-resort. W5-GATED (numeric trigger: per-cell Encrypt/Decrypt QPS or HSM-partition throughput ceiling): bespoke enclave-replicated key service (Azure-Managed-HSM pattern, 3 replicas, attested mTLS, SEV-SNP/TPM measured-boot, confidential self-healing).

LAYER 0.5 SECRETS + WORKLOAD IDENTITY (depends on KMS root): oya-kms internal CA mints SPIFFE-style mTLS workload certs at pod admission (fetch-fail=deploy-fail); cloud-secrets dynamic-secret leasing behind OpenBao API compat; KDF-derived session/cache keys. FD-001 FULL-DEPTH SLICE: zero static secrets in images/env/buck2 fabric; every pod gets a unique cert for audit/revocation; DB/Pulsar creds are leased. This breaks the KMS<->DB cycle the Vault/Google way: identity is derived/minted, not stored, so no substrate dependency loops back into KMS.

LAYER 1 NETWORK/DNS (depends on KMS+identity for mTLS, MUST precede every other serving substrate): cloud-network-dns authoritative DNS (W0-critical, serves from CAS snapshots — but at bootstrap from a static seed-config snapshot since CAS isn't up yet) + cloud-network L4 (Katran-Rust) + L7 (GFE-Rust) + mesh-library. FD-001 FULL-DEPTH SLICE: anycast DNS with shuffle-shard-of-4 + minimum-viable-answer floor + fail-static dataplane; L4/L7 multi-tenant cells with zonal independence; ALTS-model east-west mTLS on by default; in-process Cedar at the mesh+gateway. BOOTSTRAP NOTE: DNS seed-config snapshot is hand-signed for the bootstrap cell; CAS-sourced snapshots take over once Layer 4 is up. W5-GATED (clone/fan-out-class triggers): server-native NIC/DPU offload of the L4 dataplane and PSP wire-format offload — design the flow-table abstraction so this is a backend swap.

LAYER 2 PERSISTENCE (depends on KMS for envelope encryption, identity+network for mTLS routing): oya-data multi-Raft distributed-SQL (PROVEN CRDB/TiKV-class transitional impl behind the owned interface) + placement driver (separate consensus service). FD-001 FULL-DEPTH SLICE: leader-per-range, RU-style admission + GAC, F1 online schema change, transactional outbox table, CDC change-streams, HLC behind ClockSource trait on NTP-grade sync, witness/log-only replicas. Bootstrap metastore for the control plane is a SEPARATE single-Raft KV (Aurora-on-DynamoDB precedent) so the main SQL is not self-hosting-circular at bring-up. W5-GATED (write-QPS / storage-cost / engine-format triggers): bespoke Rust Pebble-class LSM + dedicated multi-Raft log store + commit-wait external consistency when PTP/owned-time clock lands.

LAYER 3 OBJECT STORAGE / CAS (metadata depends on oya-data; provides archival back to oya-data — explicit bootstrap ADR for the recursion): cloud-storage CAS four planes (transitional impl = self-hosted S3-compatible store behind the owned oya-storage interface). FD-001 FULL-DEPTH SLICE: strong read-after-write, conditional PUT, sealed-extent durability, per-tenant BLAKE3 dedup + full-object checksums, continuous-verification scrubber plane, multipart. RECURSION BREAK: CAS metadata lives in oya-data Name/Object/Block keyspaces seeded from a small static-config instance; oya-data archives its own redo log to CAS — the seed instance bootstraps before CAS is GA. W5-GATED (durability-grade / dedup-economics triggers): bespoke ShardStore-methodology Rust chunk node (executable-model + proptest in oya-ci), LRC(12,2,2) background EC, CAS as the unified substrate under Pulsar tiered storage + DB backups + buck2 artifacts.

LAYER 4 MESSAGING/EVENTING (depends on oya-data for outbox + CAS for tiered storage): Pulsar substrate (VALIDATED transitional impl behind the thin owned client crate) + oya-queue/oya-stream/oya-bus surfaces + oya-eventing. FD-001 FULL-DEPTH SLICE: tenant-keyed namespaces, shuffle-sharded broker+bookie cells, retry-letter/DLQ/redrive, CloudEvents bus, two loss classes (never-lose billing/audit + best-effort telemetry), outbox-relay running, CAS tiered offload. This is also when CAS-sourced DNS snapshots and the audit pipeline come fully online. W5-GATED (no single numeric trigger named in research — gate on operational-burden vs throughput): bespoke Rust broker + BookKeeper-class store + embedded multi-Raft metadata (reuse oya-data multi-Raft), cutover-gated.

LAYER 5 AUDIT/COMPLIANCE (cross-cutting, depends on Pulsar transport + CAS WORM + oya-data inventory + Cedar PDP): oya/audit-chain digest chain + oya/compliance Cedar conformance packs + residency packs + Policy-Zones IFC + oya/consent-graph. FD-001 FULL-DEPTH SLICE: five-stream taxonomy from middleware, CloudTrail-grade digest chain anchored in CAS WORM, provider-access audit + fail-closed approval (operators=agents), preventive Cedar at admission + detective inventory eval, KR residency pack with drift monitoring, messenger/mail personal-professional purpose-limitation in logging-then-enforce mode, evidence automation for K-ISMS-P. NOT W5-gated — must be full-depth for FD-001 because residency/audit/purpose-limitation are launch requirements, not scale features.

LAYER 6 COMMERCIAL + EDGE SURFACE (depends on all below): oya-metering/oya-billing/oya-billing-tax/cloud-billing + cloud-finops/cloud-capacity + oya/api-gateway + cloud-marketplace + oya/developer-sdk. FD-001 FULL-DEPTH SLICE: metering pipeline (per-second measure / hourly rate / monthly invoice, FOCUS 1.2, append-only price book + line items), double-entry subledger with debits=credits + CAS-archived journal, KR-VAT + EU-OSS tax seam, in-process-Cedar fail-static gateway with Service-Control rate limiting, contract-SSOT emitters, internal dogfood chargeback through the SAME pipeline. W5-GATED: AWS-style Savings-Plans hourly greedy allocation (pure rating-time logic over the same line items — reserve FOCUS CommitmentDiscount columns now); Flux-style global joint capacity+traffic optimization (record as future ADR, not now-build).
rejected_anti_patterns: Any plaintext key/KEK/root export path, including for operators (AWS: 'no mechanism to export plaintext KMS keys'; Azure removed Microsoft from the trust boundary via SGX) — enforce the one-way door in the Rust type system, no trait/API/Debug path returns root/KEK plaintext; operator break-glass to key material is designed out, not policied out.

Central ticket/credential service on the connection hot path (Meta retired Kerberos because KDC fan-out collapsed) and static long-lived secrets in config/images/env/buck2 fabric — replaced by issuance-time identity + KDF-derived keys + leased dynamic secrets with auto-revocation.

DNS/health automation that can converge to zero or withdraw its own reachability on backend health (Meta Oct-2021 anycast withdrawal + AWS Oct-2025 DNS Enactor race, both multi-hour outages) — hard code invariant: minimum-viable-answer floor, DNS never withdraws reachability on backend health, fail static.

Per-pod sidecar proxies at fleet scale (Meta quantified hundreds-of-thousands-of-machines saved by the library model; Istio itself retreated to ambient; AWS App Mesh EOL Sept 2026) — mesh is an in-process tower library with in-process Cedar, not a sidecar.

Event-driven delta config propagation on a critical data plane and synchronous control-plane dependency on the flow/packet/serving hot path — replaced by constant-work fixed-cadence full-snapshot pull + fail-static dataplane (delta pipelines fall behind exactly during incidents).

Leaderless eventually-consistent quorums (Amazon retired the 2007 Dynamo design) and distributed consensus on the storage I/O hot path (Aurora avoids it via quorum-sets+epochs) and single-leader-for-the-whole-DB as the scale plan — multi-Raft leader-per-range with consensus reserved for reconfiguration.

Blocking/synchronous-global-membership DDL and bulk data re-encryption on key rotation — F1 online async schema change is mandatory; rotation = append-only versioned KEKs with ciphertext self-describing its version, never re-encrypt the data lake.

Eventual consistency as the object-store API default (S3 paid more in verification work than implementation to retrofit it in 2020) and single-master metadata (GFS master, retired by Colossus->Bigtable) and cross-tenant content dedup (oracle/correlated-loss blast radius — no hyperscaler ships it) and smart data nodes that know objects/buckets (Tectonic chunk store is deliberately flat) — strong-consistency designed-in, metadata in distributed SQL, per-tenant-only dedup, dumb flat chunk store.

Per-team/per-workload dedicated clusters and shared-kernel containers as a hostile-tenant boundary (Borg: 20-30% machine tax; no hyperscaler runs shared-kernel across a tenant boundary) and prod-preempts-prod and manual resource limits as default (Borg: 46%->23% slack, 10x fewer OOM with autopilot) — one shared fleet, microVM per tenant workload, priced priority bands, predictive autoscaling.

Billing off the observability/metrics pipeline (AWS SaaS doctrine: METERING != METRICS), mutable usage records / editable SKU definitions post-publish, unbounded late-event acceptance, budgets/alerts as spend enforcement (GCP: budgets never cap; quota enforces / billing observes), synchronous per-request billing writes, and monolithic RDBMS as the financial ledger (Amazon retired Oracle FLASH) — append-only line items + immutable price book + bounded lateness + double-entry subledger.

End-to-end exactly-once claims across heterogeneous systems and 2PC across services (Kafka transactions stop at the cluster boundary) and global/total ordering (nobody offers it) and partitioned provisioned 'lite' messaging tiers (Google deprecated Pub/Sub Lite) and external coordination quorums as broker metadata (Kafka removed ZooKeeper; Pulsar->Oxia) and raw broker endpoints exposed to tenants — at-least-once + outbox + idempotent consumer, per-key ordering only, embedded multi-Raft metadata, authenticated axum surfaces.

Hand-maintained OpenAPI as the master spec (Microsoft deprecated OpenAPI-first July 2026; AWS never let it be source), synchronous global quota/entitlement checks on the request hot path, gateway quotas as billing enforcement, nginx-based gateway data planes (Google retired ESPv1 for Envoy), and manual human-in-the-loop marketplace fulfillment (all clouds made webhook+metering integration a certification requirement) — typed model is source / OpenAPI is emitted, local-cache+async-reconcile quotas, Envoy operating model, integration-test-as-listing-review.

Best-effort/droppable audit delivery, mutable or DB-ACL-trusted audit stores, post-hoc audits as the primary privacy control (Meta moved to inline IFC), physical data segregation per purpose (Meta rejected as cost-prohibitive), hierarchical/complex label taxonomies (Meta retired for flat independent GDAs), 90-day default audit retention (Microsoft raised to 180 after Storm-0558; GCP bar is 400-day non-deletable), and residency as a retrofit (Microsoft's 3-year thousands-of-engineers EU Data Boundary) — never-drop digest-chained WORM audit, inline Policy-Zones IFC, flat labels, >=400-day admin retention, region/realm immutable in resource IDs from day one.
prescription.dogfood_bootstrap_order: STEP 0 (root-of-trust ceremony) -> Shamir M-of-N offline-root split + dual-control geo-separated safes, executed as a versioned runbook (cloud-kms/runbooks/key-material-quorum-loss.md already exists as the ceremony seed). STEP 1 (KMS unseal) -> oya-kms (cloud-kms) auto-unsealed via OpenBao + PKCS#11 FIPS-L3 pair; KMS storage = its own minimal LOCAL Raft group, NOT oya-data, breaking the KMS<->DB cycle; root key in RAM across a peer-distributor set. STEP 2 (secrets + workload identity) -> oya-kms internal CA mints SPIFFE mTLS certs at pod admission (oya/identity/workload-identity) + cloud-secrets leases dynamic creds behind OpenBao API compat + KDF-derived session/cache keys (identity is minted/derived, never stored, so nothing loops back into KMS). STEP 3 (identity/IAM) -> cloud-iam + oya/oya-identity bind human/agent principals and tenant entities to the workload-identity chain. STEP 4 (PDP) -> Cedar policy-decision point: per-service cedar/policies (cloud-kms/cedar/policies.cedar pattern) loaded into the in-process cedar-policy crate at the mesh+gateway (libs/oya-governance-cedar-coverage + oya/policy) — key authz, API authz, and admission authz are all Cedar from this point. STEP 5 (network/DNS) -> cloud-network-dns authoritative DNS from a hand-signed BOOTSTRAP SEED snapshot (CAS not yet up) + cloud-network L4 (Katran-Rust) + L7 (GFE-Rust) + mesh-library with ALTS-model mTLS using STEP-2 certs; fail-static dataplane + minimum-answer floor invariants active. STEP 6 (persistence) -> oya-data multi-Raft distributed-SQL (PROVEN CRDB/TiKV-class transitional impl, cloud-data) envelope-encrypted via STEP-1 KMS; control-plane bootstrap metastore is a SEPARATE single-Raft KV so the main SQL is not self-hosting-circular. STEP 7 (object/CAS) -> cloud-storage CAS (transitional S3-compatible impl), metadata in oya-data Name/Object/Block keyspaces seeded from a small static-config instance (explicit recursion-break ADR); oya-data then begins redo-log archival to CAS and DNS switches from seed-snapshot to CAS-sourced signed zone snapshots. STEP 8 (messaging) -> Pulsar substrate (cloud + oya/eventing) with oya-queue/oya-stream/oya-bus surfaces, outbox-relay from oya-data, CAS tiered-storage offload, two loss classes. STEP 9 (audit/compliance) -> oya/audit-chain digest chain anchored in CAS WORM + five-stream taxonomy from tower middleware + oya/compliance Cedar conformance + KR residency pack + messenger/mail Policy-Zones purpose-limitation (logging-mode-first) + provider-access audit/approval (operators=agents). STEP 10 (commercial/edge) -> oya-metering/oya-billing/oya-billing-tax + cloud-finops/cloud-capacity quota + oya/api-gateway (in-process Cedar, fail-static, Service-Control rate limiting) + cloud-marketplace + oya/developer-sdk; internal dogfood chargeback for every oya/*+cloud/* service flows through the SAME metering pipeline from this step. FD-001 (tenancy+RBAC core + messenger/mail/community + ops-dashboard + KR localization pack) then sits on the full stack with no placeholder substrate.
open_questions: Numeric cutover triggers per substrate are NOT yet authored (only ADR-0510's SCM triggers exist). Founder ruling needed on the threshold table for each W5-gated substrate mirroring ADR-0510's format: oya-data (write-QPS / storage-cost-per-TB / engine-format-rev forcing the bespoke LSM), CAS (durability-grade or dedup-economics forcing ShardStore-Rust), oya-kms (per-cell Encrypt/Decrypt QPS or HSM-partition throughput forcing the enclave service), Pulsar (the research names no single numeric trigger — is operational-burden-vs-throughput an acceptable qualitative gate, or must a number be invented?). Without these numbers each 'cutover-gated' becomes a silent 'deferred' — the exact failure ADR-0510 rejects.

Clock hardware decision point: the ClockSource trait launches on NTP-grade sync with uncertainty-restarts, but commit-wait external consistency (the Spanner property) requires PTP/owned-time bounds. Does FD-001 tenancy+RBAC need true external consistency, or is serializable-with-uncertainty-restart sufficient for v1? AWS Time Sync proves microsecond bounds are commodity — is owned-time-fabric a W2 or a W5 item?

HSM hardware acquisition: the transitional root-sealing layer needs a small FIPS-140-3-L3 device pair (PKCS#11). Is procuring physical HSMs in scope for the dogfood, or does the bootstrap root ceremony run on a software-FIPS module + OpenBao seal-wrap until physical custody hardware is acquired? This gates whether STEP 0/1 is fully real or itself transitionally-impl'd.

Firecracker adopt-vs-reimplement: the matrix treats Firecracker as the rare 'reimplement = adopt the proven Rust artifact' case via a bespoke runtime shim. Founder confirmation needed that adopting Apache-2.0 Firecracker (not a from-scratch Rust VMM) satisfies bespoke-over-OSS doctrine, and whether the same logic extends to BookKeeper-shape storage and the OpenBao wrap layer (i.e., where exactly is the adopt/reimplement line for proven-Rust vs proven-non-Rust artifacts?).

CAS recursion bootstrap ADR is named but not written: oya-data metadata seeds CAS while oya-data archives to CAS. The Colossus/Bigtable precedent uses a small static-config seed instance, but the exact seeding mechanism, the failure-recovery story if the seed instance is lost before CAS is GA, and whether the seed instance is itself KMS-encrypted (it must decrypt before CAS exists) need a versioned ADR before STEP 6/7.

Per-tenant KEK economics at FD-001 scale: mandatory per-tenant KEK enables GDPR crypto-shred but multiplies KEK count by tenant count. At what tenant cardinality does the per-cell key-token table rewrite (daily domain-key rotation) stop being a metadata-scale batch job? Need the KEK-count ceiling per cell and the sharding strategy for the key-token table.

Messenger/mail purpose-limitation enforcement timing: Policy-Zones launches logging-mode-first then enforce. For FD-001 with the personal/professional split as a LAUNCH requirement, does the KR/EU residency+privacy posture permit shipping in logging-mode (detect, don't block) at GA, or must enforcement-mode (auto-block unremediated flows) be live at FD-001 exit? This changes whether the IFC enforcement points in the shared data-access crate are blocking-path-critical for v1.

Tax content provider for KR launch: the matrix ships KR-VAT native + EU non-Union-OSS native with an Avalara/Stripe-Tax adapter slot. Confirmation that native KR-VAT (Simplified Business Operator Registration, quarterly filing, no input-VAT credit) is correct to hand-implement for FD-001's KR launch rather than starting on the Avalara adapter — i.e., is KR-VAT simple enough to be the one exception to 'never reimplement tax content', or should even KR ride a content provider?
